clue.text: Never satisfied with banalities at a resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters of the word before are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at a holiday resort is never content with the trite chatter around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday place but is read as re-sort, rearranging BANALITIES; 'with' and 'at a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can never be filled or contented is greedy beyond limit, which is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Not where those called to the bar obtain their refreshers, however

definitions.text: Not where those called to the bar obtain their refreshers, however

parts.words: Not where those called to the bar obtain their refreshers, however
parts.note: barristers are called to the bar at the ... of Court, not these older lawyers' houses; refreshers are a barrister's extra fees but also drinks, and ... serve drinks

explanation.surface: A remark about where newly qualified barristers go for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Chancery were old London societies for lawyers, distinct from the Inns of Court that call barristers to the bar; 'refreshers' plays on a barrister's daily fee and a drink at an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: These historic legal societies sound like pubs but were never the bodies that admitted barristers, so the clue says where such people do not get their refreshment.

clue.text: Getting pleasure from our inclusive price-cut

indicators.note: a price-cut that is inclusive of something holds it inside, so the word before goes within

parts.note: a saving is a cut in what you pay
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper enjoys a discount that is all-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclusive' signals a container: the price-cut takes in the possessive word.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish or enjoy something is to take delight in it, as when tasting food slowly.

clue.text: Accommodating notice 5 is out to find

indicators.note: with the letters of the little word taken out, what is left of the referenced answer is jumbled into the new word

parts.note: the answer to 5 down, a figure of speech of understatement

explanation.surface: A sign about lodging that must be found once something is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of IS out of LITOTES (the answer to 5) and rearrange the remaining L, T, O, T, E; 'out' signals both the removal and the jumble, 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign offering rooms or a property for rent is a notice about available lodging.

clue.text: Sailor did wrong, we hear, to cut off

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, an ordinary sailor

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound-alike, so the spelling entered differs from the spoken word

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong, so did wrong is sinned

explanation.surface: A sailor misbehaves and is to be cut off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: SCIND is said like 'sinned'; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare verb means to sever or remove by cutting, from Latin abscindere.

clue.text: Untruthful about drink? That's an understatement

indicators.note: the falsehoods wrap around the drink, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: untruthful statements are lies
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Accusing a drinker of fibbing about how much they had would be putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The definition is the whole phrase: the answer is the name for such an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhetorical figure affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad', a classic form of understatement.

clue.text: Roughly handle a beetle

definitions.meaning: to treat roughly, to batter or paw at
a beetle is also a heavy wooden mallet, a sense shared with the answer

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to manhandle, and the noun is a heavy hammer, which a beetle also is.

clue.text: By way of being an enclosure for the birdlike

indicators.note: the following word is described as acting as the container
a little word that is an enclosure surrounds the piece named first

parts.note: taken as written
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A route that serves as a pen for something resembling a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being an enclosure for' says the article wraps round the route word; 'the' before 'birdlike' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or resembling birds, from Latin avis.

clue.text: Utterly boring, yearned to turn in

indicators.note: the turning piece goes in the middle of the yearning word

parts.note: to long is to yearn, so yearned is longed
to wind is to turn, as a handle or a road does

explanation.surface: Someone who longed for something now feels it twisting inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the hyphenated answer means talking at tedious length.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker who goes on at tedious length is tiresome, so the compound adjective describes dull verbosity.

clue.text: Careful about extravagant speech in a pledge

indicators.note: the cautious word goes round the outburst, holding it inside

parts.note: wary means cautious, careful
a rant is a wild, ranting speech

explanation.surface: Being cautious about grand talk when giving a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'in a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee, as given on goods, is a formal promise or assurance.

clue.text: Unusual state of affairs fiction writers exploit

definitions.meaning: a new and unfamiliar set of circumstances
a set-up from a book of fiction, which authors use as a plot

explanation.definitionFit: A fresh, unprecedented circumstance; read literally, a scenario in a work of fiction that authors develop.

clue.text: See 10
With whom one doesn't play solo

definitions.text: With whom one doesn't play solo

parts.words: With whom one doesn't play solo
parts.note: describes a partner in music for two, someone you perform with rather than alone

explanation.surface: A description of a musical partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in a two-part piece always has a partner, so playing with one means not performing alone.

clue.text: Point we're wrong about; so start again

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed round the compass point
letters gone wrong are put into a new order

parts.note: the contraction gives the letters W, E, R, E
N is north, a compass point

explanation.surface: Admitting a mistake on a point and resolving to begin afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns WERE into REEW, which goes 'about' N; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume or begin something over again, as with a contract or an effort.

clue.text: See 1
Used a ploy that sounded feeble

indicators.note: the clue says the word spoken resembles another, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to faint in the old sense is to grow weak, so feeble here stands for fainted, grown faint

explanation.surface: Someone tried a trick that sounded weak.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is said like 'fainted', which the setter takes from 'feeble'; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a deceptive move, as a boxer drawing a guard, is to use a ruse.

clue.text: Dote upon, that's certain, at any rate to begin with

indicators.note: the jumbled rate is placed at the start, ahead of the certainty
any arrangement of the letters is allowed, so the word after is jumbled

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone is sure, at least for now, that they adore something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'any' signals the jumble of 'rate', and 'to begin with' places that jumble first; 'that's' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish or prize someone dearly is to adore them.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing role for Chopin, by George!

definitions.text: Sleep-inducing role for Chopin, by George!

parts.words: Sleep-inducing role for Chopin, by George!
parts.note: the novelist George Sand was Chopin's lover, so he was her man; the folklore figure brings sleep with sand in the eyes

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a part the composer played.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand, the French novelist, was Chopin's partner; 'by George!' doubles as the old exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of nursery lore sprinkles grains in children's eyes to send them to sleep, and Chopin was literally the man of Sand.

clue.text: Mineral emanating from a different source

indicators.note: the letters come from somewhere else, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A mineral giving off something that came from elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange EMANATING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grey-black ore of manganese, a mineral of manganese oxide hydroxide.

clue.text: Most eminent sight he recollected

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered up again into a new order

explanation.surface: A man remembers the view he saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered but means collected again, rearranging SIGHT HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of high, it means loftiest or of top rank.

clue.text: Roman poet from recent organisation with energy

indicators.note: the letters are given a new organisation, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A classical writer emerges from a new body with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges RECENT into TERENC; 'from' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Terentius Afer was a Roman comic playwright, whose verse comedies count him among Latin poets.

clue.text: Place on any tour within Basque limits

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the outer pair
the limits of a word are its first and last letters
a tour moves around, so the letters are taken round into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip that stays inside the Basque border.
explanation.walkthrough: B and E, the first and last letters of 'Basque', hold AYONN, made by the 'tour' of ON ANY. The town is in the French Basque country.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in south-west France, in the Basque region, is a location.

clue.text: Conceited boss, maybe

definitions.meaning: a boss could be called the top person, the leader at the head of things

explanation.definitionFit: A swollen-headed person is vain; read as two words, a leader in charge is a senior chief.

clue.text: British linesman of sound hearing

indicators.note: on hearing, the spoken word resembles the name, which is spelt differently

parts.note: noise is sound

explanation.surface: A British official at a match with good ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes, author of 'The Highwayman', was a British poet; a 'linesman' is a writer of lines of verse, not a football official.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet writes lines, so a British versifier is jokingly a linesman.

clue.text: Sing at the top of the scale

definitions.text: Sing at the top of the scale

parts.words: Sing at the top of the scale
parts.note: describes Alpine singing that flips into a high falsetto, and is done high up in the mountains

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing very high notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine style of singing swaps rapidly between chest voice and high falsetto, and is done on the heights.

clue.text: Fitting course of action as Tories see it

definitions.meaning: the Tories are the political right, so their way is the right's path

explanation.definitionFit: The correct method; also the path of the political right, which Conservatives follow.

clue.text: Tom is up to it, but mum's the word

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word that is up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom is up to something, but keeping quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reverses CAT to TAC; 'to' and 'but' are links. 'Mum's the word' means say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspoken or implied without words, as silence is when someone keeps quiet.

clue.text: Join provided a start is given

indicators.note: the letter is given the start position, placed before the other piece

parts.note: but can mean except that or unless, the condition introduced by provided

explanation.surface: Agreeing to join on condition of a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: A is placed at the start, before BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on or be adjacent to, so two things touch along an edge.

clue.text: Quality best in the long run

definitions.text: Quality best in the long run

parts.words: Quality best in the long run
parts.note: describes the stamina that matters in distance running and in lasting out over time

explanation.surface: A remark that some virtue pays off eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power is the quality most needed in a marathon or any long trial.

clue.text: C on front member on the scale

indicators.note: the letter is put on the front of the following piece

parts.note: a limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A letter put before a body part, on the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes in front of LIMB; 'on the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend a wall or mountain is to go up it by climbing.

clue.text: A cry from the Shetlands, perhaps

definitions.meaning: one of the Shetland Islands, north of Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: A loud shout; also the name of the second largest of the Shetland Islands, off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Meal prepared for a healthy appetite

definitions.text: Meal prepared for a healthy appetite

parts.words: Meal prepared for a healthy appetite
parts.note: describes food made in advance, needing no cooking, and also someone hungry and eager for food

explanation.surface: A dish made for a hungry diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sold already cooked needs no preparation; a person with a good appetite is also eager to tuck in.
